collection.credit:
NEW EVENTS — PONDERING HOW LIFE HAS GONE (LIF-01..50, draft for the owner, 2026-11-15)
Adults of every age looking at their own lives so far: roads not taken, quiet satisfaction, small regrets, unexpected pride, things left unfinished, luck, gratitude and plenty of amusement. Nobody has to reach a verdict.
Written in the style of the owner's own events. Edit anything and send it back; nothing ships until you approve.

ledger.why: the casting line, carried out as the roles' ages (picks an elder and a child aged 6-13)

collection.description: An elder who never learned to dive deep sees a child bring up a shell: say it is wonderful, or ask what it is like.

setup.name: The setup
setup.text: When (subject) was young, (subject.he/she) always meant to learn to dive deep, all the way to the bottom of the bay, where the big shells are. (subject.He/she) never got round to it. Now (subject.his/her) lungs and ears won't let (subject.him/her). (subject.He/she) knows it's too late. Today (friend) comes up from the water triumphant, holding a big shell from the very bottom.

o1.name: Outcome A
o1.text: (subject) tells (friend) it's the best shell (friend.he/she) has ever seen, and means it. (friend) asks if (subject) ever dived that deep. "No," says (subject). "I always meant to." (friend) thinks about this, then gives (subject.him/her) the shell. "Now you've got one from the bottom." (subject) is very touched. It isn't the same. It's something else, and it's good.

o2.name: Outcome B
o2.text: (subject) asks what it's like down there. (friend) describes it all: the cold, the quiet, the light turning green, the big shells lying in the sand. (subject) listens with (subject.his/her) eyes closed. It's a little sad, knowing (subject.he/she) will never see it. It's also lovely, hearing it. Both at once. (subject.He/she) asks (friend) to tell (subject.him/her) again next time.
